title: 🗺️ Map & Diagram Labelling

sections.heading: What it tests
sections.body:
Map labelling: you see a map with some labelled features and empty spaces. You hear a description of the location and must label the empty features.

Diagram labelling: you see a diagram of a process, machine, or object. You hear an explanation and label the parts.

sections.heading: Map strategy
sections.body:
Before listening:
• Study the map carefully
• Note what's already labelled (these give you reference points)
• Identify the compass directions if shown

While listening:
• Follow the speaker's route mentally
• Listen for directional language: opposite, next to, adjacent to, to the north of, facing, between, past
• Match what you hear to what you see on the map

highlight: The speaker will describe locations relative to already-labelled features. Use those landmarks as anchors. If lost, skip and return — questions are in order.

question: Which phrase means "directly across from"?
explanation:
"Opposite" = directly across from, facing.

"Adjacent to", "next to", and "beside" all mean BESIDE/NEXT TO (touching or very close).

In map questions, this distinction is crucial. "The library is opposite the bank" = they face each other across a road/space.

instruction: Match each direction phrase to its meaning:

pairs.meaning: at the point where two roads cross

explanation: Map labelling questions use precise spatial language. Recognising these instantly — without needing to translate — is the difference between Band 6 and Band 8 in listening.

question: On a map, a building is described as "past the café, on the left, before you reach the roundabout." If you're walking north, where is it?
options: North-east of the café, west of the roundabout
West of the café, south of the roundabout
correct: North-east of the café, west of the roundabout
explanation:
Walking NORTH → left = WEST, right = EAST
Past the café (further north)
Before the roundabout (south of it)

So: north of café + west side + before roundabout = north-west of café area, west of roundabout.

Always mentally orient yourself in the direction the speaker is describing.

question: You need to label a building on a map. You've missed the description. What should you do?
options: Leave it blank and move on
Go back and re-listen to the whole section
Make your best guess from context then move on
correct: Make your best guess from context then move on
explanation:
In the real test, you CANNOT re-listen. So:
1. Make a reasonable guess based on what you've heard
2. Move on immediately — don't freeze
3. Use the 10-minute transfer time to revisit and confirm

Blank answers score 0. A guess has a chance of being right. There's no penalty for wrong answers in IELTS.
